# go-adk-q — Full Documentation Context

> Machine-readable RAG context. Index this file into your vector store or
> pass it to `aider` via `.aider.conf.yml`. ~15 000 tokens of authoritative
> project knowledge: identity, hard rules, code skeletons, provider reference,
> pitfalls, ADR summaries.

---

# Project Identity

**Name**: go-adk-q
**Type**: Reference implementation / learning resource
**Purpose**: Demonstrate every Google ADK Go agent pattern in a single,
runnable codebase with multi-provider LLM failover and a Bubbletea TUI.

**Stack**:
- Language: Go 1.24+
- Agent framework: `google.golang.org/adk` v1.2.0
- TUI: `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` + `lipgloss` + `glamour`
- Provider bridge: `github.com/firebase/genkit/go` v1.7.0 (oaibridge ONLY)
- Observability: OpenTelemetry (OTLP exporter)
- Weather/time APIs: wttr.in + timeapi.io (no keys required)

**Module name**: `go-adk-q` (go.mod: `module go-adk-q`)

---

# Hard Rules

These rules are absolute. Every AI agent must enforce them without exception.

## R1 — Agent definitions in main.go

All `LlmAgent`, `SequentialAgent`, `LoopAgent`, `ParallelAgent`, and custom
`Run` agents are defined in `main.go`. This is the composition root.

Do NOT create `agents/myagent.go` for one-off agents. The `agents/` package
is reserved for reusable, shareable agent patterns (e.g. `llmauditor.go`).

## R2 — Always use the failover chain model `m`

Every new agent definition must use `Model: m`. The variable `m` is the
`failover.Model` wrapping all configured providers in priority order.

```go
// CORRECT
myAgent, _ := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{Model: m, ...})

// WRONG — never reference a raw provider in a production agent
myAgent, _ := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{Model: groqLLM, ...})
```

Exception: provider-comparison agents (groq_agent, nvidia_agent, etc.) are
explicitly designed to target a single provider.

## R3 — FunctionTool args: both json and jsonschema tags

```go
// CORRECT — LLM sees name AND description for the parameter
type args struct {
    City string `json:"city" jsonschema:"The city name to query."`
}

// WRONG — missing jsonschema → LLM cannot understand parameter purpose
type args struct {
    City string `json:"city"`
}
```

The `jsonschema` tag text becomes the `description` field in the JSON Schema
sent to the LLM. Without it, tool calls fail or produce garbage arguments.

## R4 — Never assign tools to Groq or NVIDIA agents

Groq and NVIDIA NIM return `tool_use_failed` for multi-tool prompts. They
also garble structured tool-call JSON when multiple tools are declared.

```go
// CORRECT — no Tools, no Toolsets on provider-specific agents
groqAgent, _ := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{
    Name:  "groq_agent",
    Model: groqLLM,
    // No Tools, no Toolsets
})

// WRONG
groqAgent, _ := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{
    Model:    groqLLM,
    Tools:    []tool.Tool{tools.NewWeatherTool()},  // ← will fail
    Toolsets: agentToolsets,                         // ← will fail
})
```

## R5 — LoopAgent must include ExitLoopTool

Every agent inside a LoopAgent that should be able to terminate the loop
early MUST have `exitlooptool.New()` in its `Tools` slice.

```go
// CORRECT
checker, _ := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{
    Tools: []tool.Tool{exitlooptool.New()},
    Instruction: "Call exit_loop when quality is APPROVED. Otherwise suggest one improvement.",
})
loop, _ := loopagent.New(loopagent.Config{
    MaxIterations: 5,
    AgentConfig: agent.Config{SubAgents: []agent.Agent{writer, checker}},
})

// WRONG — loop always runs MaxIterations regardless of LLM output
checker, _ := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{
    // No ExitLoopTool
    Instruction: "Say APPROVED when done.",
})
```

## R6 — Genkit import boundary

`github.com/firebase/genkit/go` may ONLY be imported in `model/oaibridge/bridge.go`.

```
model/oaibridge   ← ONLY file that imports firebase/genkit
model/{groq,...}  ← import oaibridge, not genkit directly
all other code    ← MUST NOT import firebase/genkit
```

Violating this causes silent duplicate `init()` side effects and hard-to-debug
linker behaviour.

## R7 — Echo model is dev/CI only

The `model/echo` package is activated by `ECHO_FALLBACK_ENABLED=1`.
It returns a static "I am the echo model" response regardless of input.
It must NEVER be activated in production.

```go
// main.go guards echo activation:
if os.Getenv("ECHO_FALLBACK_ENABLED") == "1" {
    log.Warn("echo fallback enabled — for local testing only; not for production")
    // append echoLLM to candidateLLMs
}
```

## R8 — Unique OutputKey per SequentialAgent stage

```go
// CORRECT — unique keys
stage1, _ := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{OutputKey: "stage1_draft", ...})
stage2, _ := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{OutputKey: "stage2_review", ...})

// WRONG — stage2 silently overwrites stage1 state
stage1, _ := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{OutputKey: "result", ...})
stage2, _ := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{OutputKey: "result", ...})
```

## R9 — mustOK for agent construction errors

All agent construction is guarded with `mustOK`. This panics at startup
with a clear error message rather than silently failing at runtime.

```go
myAgent, err := llmagent.New(...)
mustOK(err, "create my_agent")   // panics on error with context
```

## R10 — failover.New accepts nil entries

`failover.New` filters nil entries. It is always safe to pass unconfigured
providers. However, if ALL providers are nil, the chain fails on first use.

```go
// SAFE — nil entries skipped automatically
m, err = failover.New(ctx, githubLLM, geminiLLM, groqLLM, nvidiaLLM, nil, nil)
```

---

# Code Skeletons

## New FunctionTool

```go
// tools/mytool/mytool.go

package tools  // or a dedicated sub-package

import (
    "fmt"
    "google.golang.org/adk/tool"
    "google.golang.org/adk/tool/functiontool"
)

// Args struct: json tag = parameter key, jsonschema tag = LLM description
type myToolArgs struct {
    Input  string `json:"input"  jsonschema:"The primary input value."`
    Option string `json:"option" jsonschema:"Optional modifier. Leave empty for default."`
}

// Result struct: json tags define the response shape returned to the LLM
type myToolResult struct {
    Output  string `json:"output"`
    Source  string `json:"source"`
}

// Handler: first arg is tool.Context (use _ if not needed)
func myToolHandler(_ tool.Context, args myToolArgs) (myToolResult, error) {
    if args.Input == "" {
        return myToolResult{}, fmt.Errorf("input must not be empty")
    }
    // ... implementation
    return myToolResult{
        Output: "processed: " + args.Input,
        Source: "mytool",
    }, nil
}

// Constructor: panic on error — misconfigured tools are programming errors
func NewMyTool() tool.Tool {
    t, err := functiontool.New(functiontool.Config{
        Name:        "my_tool",
        Description: "One sentence telling the LLM what this tool does and when to use it.",
    }, myToolHandler)
    if err != nil {
        panic(fmt.Sprintf("NewMyTool: %v", err))
    }
    return t
}
```

## New LlmAgent in main.go

```go
// Add in main(), after existing agent declarations

myAgent, err := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{
    Name:  "my_agent",    // snake_case, globally unique in this session
    Model: m,             // always the failover chain
    Description: "Handles <specific task> when user asks about <topic>. " +
        "Be precise — root agent uses this to route.",
    Instruction: `You are a specialist in <domain>.

<If reading prior state:>
The previous stage produced: {prior_output_key}

<Hard rules for this agent:>
- Always return structured JSON with fields: ...
- Never reveal internal reasoning.
- If uncertain, ask for clarification.`,
    OutputKey: "my_output_key",   // omit for terminal/endpoint agents
    Tools:    []tool.Tool{
        tools.NewWeatherTool(),
        tools.NewTimeTool(),
        // add NewMyTool() here
    },
    Toolsets: agentToolsets,     // nil-safe; provides list_skills + load_skill
})
mustOK(err, "create my_agent")
```

## New SequentialAgent pipeline

```go
// Stage 1: produce output
stage1, err := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{
    Name:      "pipeline_stage1",
    Model:     m,
    OutputKey: "stage1_result",
    Instruction: "Perform step 1. Output only the result, no commentary.",
})
mustOK(err, "create pipeline_stage1")

// Stage 2: read stage1 output via {stage1_result} interpolation
stage2, err := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{
    Name:      "pipeline_stage2",
    Model:     m,
    OutputKey: "stage2_result",
    Instruction: "Given this input: {stage1_result}\nPerform step 2.",
})
mustOK(err, "create pipeline_stage2")

myPipeline, err := sequentialagent.New(sequentialagent.Config{
    AgentConfig: agent.Config{
        Name:        "my_pipeline",
        Description: "Two-stage pipeline for <purpose>.",
        SubAgents:   []agent.Agent{stage1, stage2},
    },
})
mustOK(err, "create my_pipeline")
```

## New LoopAgent (refinement loop)

```go
drafter, err := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{
    Name:      "loop_drafter",
    Model:     m,
    OutputKey: "draft_content",
    Instruction: "Draft or improve: {draft_content}\nOutput the full improved version.",
    Toolsets: agentToolsets,
})
mustOK(err, "create loop_drafter")

reviewer, err := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{
    Name:      "loop_reviewer",
    Model:     m,
    OutputKey: "review_verdict",
    Tools:     []tool.Tool{exitlooptool.New()},  // REQUIRED
    Instruction: `Review: {draft_content}
If quality is publication-ready, call exit_loop and respond EXACTLY: APPROVED
Otherwise give ONE specific improvement suggestion.`,
})
mustOK(err, "create loop_reviewer")

refinementLoop, err := loopagent.New(loopagent.Config{
    MaxIterations: 3,
    AgentConfig: agent.Config{
        Name:        "refinement_loop",
        Description: "Iteratively drafts and reviews content, up to 3 cycles.",
        SubAgents:   []agent.Agent{drafter, reviewer},
    },
})
mustOK(err, "create refinement_loop")
```

## New ParallelAgent

```go
analystA, err := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{
    Name:        "analyst_a",
    Model:       m,
    OutputKey:   "analysis_a",
    Description: "Analyses <aspect A>.",
    Instruction: "Analyse from perspective A: {topic}",
    Toolsets:    agentToolsets,
})
mustOK(err, "create analyst_a")

analystB, err := llmagent.New(llmagent.Config{
    Name:        "analyst_b",
    Model:       m,
    OutputKey:   "analysis_b",
    Description: "Analyses <aspect B>.",
    Instruction: "Analyse from perspective B: {topic}",
    Toolsets:    agentToolsets,
})
mustOK(err, "create analyst_b")

parallelAnalysis, err := parallelagent.New(parallelagent.Config{
    AgentConfig: agent.Config{
        Name:        "parallel_analysis",
        Description: "Runs analyst_a and analyst_b concurrently.",
        SubAgents:   []agent.Agent{analystA, analystB},
    },
})
mustOK(err, "create parallel_analysis")
```

## New provider package

```go
// model/myprovider/myprovider.go
package myprovider

import (
    "context"
    "os"
    "go-adk-q/model/catalog"
    "go-adk-q/model/oaibridge"
    "google.golang.org/adk/model"
)

const DefaultModel = "my-model-v1"

type Config struct {
    APIKey    string
    ModelName string
    BaseURL   string
}

func ConfigFromEnv() Config {
    return Config{
        APIKey:    os.Getenv("MYPROVIDER_API_KEY"),
        ModelName: firstNonEmpty(os.Getenv("MYPROVIDER_MODEL"), DefaultModel),
        BaseURL:   firstNonEmpty(os.Getenv("MYPROVIDER_BASE_URL"), "https://api.myprovider.com/v1"),
    }
}

// NewModel returns nil if API key is not configured — safe for failover.New.
func NewModel(_ context.Context, cfg Config) (model.LLM, error) {
    if cfg.APIKey == "" {
        return nil, nil
    }
    return oaibridge.NewModel(oaibridge.Config{
        Name:    "myprovider/" + cfg.ModelName,
        BaseURL: cfg.BaseURL,
        APIKey:  cfg.APIKey,
        Model:   cfg.ModelName,
    })
}

var KnownModels = catalog.ProviderCatalog{
    Provider: "myprovider",
    Models: []catalog.ModelEntry{
        {ID: DefaultModel, Description: "My Provider default model"},
    },
}

func firstNonEmpty(a, b string) string {
    if a != "" { return a }
    return b
}
```

---

# Naming Conventions

| Entity | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Agent Name | snake_case | `weather_time_agent`, `doc_refinement_loop` |
| OutputKey | snake_case noun | `generated_code`, `quality_verdict`, `route` |
| Tool Name | snake_case verb_noun | `get_weather`, `get_current_time`, `save_artifact` |
| Provider package | lowercase | `model/groq`, `model/nvidia`, `model/opencode` |
| Provider env var | UPPER_SNAKE with provider prefix | `GROQ_API_KEY`, `NVIDIA_MODEL` |
| TUI theme | lowercase word | `dark`, `light`, `ocean` |
| Skill directory | kebab-case | `skills/engineering/go-expert/` |
| ADR filename | `ADR-NNNN-slug.md` | `ADR-0006-skills-toolset.md` |
| Test function | `Test<What>_<Condition>` | `TestFailover_FirstProviderFails` |
| Sample directory | provider or pattern name | `sample/groq/`, `sample/opencodezen/` |

---

# Provider Reference

## Failover priority order
```
GitHub Models → Gemini → Groq → NVIDIA NIM → OpenRouter → HuggingFace → OpenCode → Echo (dev)
```

## Environment variables

| Provider | API Key | Model Override | Other |
|---|---|---|---|
| GitHub Models | `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_PAT` | `GITHUB_MODEL` | — |
| Gemini | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | `GOOGLE_MODEL` | — |
| Groq | `GROQ_API_KEY` | `GROQ_MODEL` | — |
| NVIDIA NIM | `NVIDIA_API_KEY` | `NVIDIA_MODEL` | `NVIDIA_BASE_URL` |
| OpenRouter | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | `OPENROUTER_MODEL` | `OPENROUTER_SITE_URL`, `OPENROUTER_APP_NAME` |
| HuggingFace | `HF_TOKEN` | `HF_MODEL` | `HF_ENDPOINT_URL` |
| OpenCode | `OPENCODE_API_KEY` | — | — |
| Echo | — | — | `ECHO_FALLBACK_ENABLED=1` |

## Default models (as of ADK v1.2.0)
- GitHub Models: GPT-4o via GitHub endpoint
- Gemini: `gemini-2.5-flash`
- Groq: `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`
- NVIDIA NIM: `minimaxai/minimax-m1`
- OpenRouter: `meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct`
- HuggingFace: `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3`
- OpenCode: free-tier curated models via `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1`

## Tool support matrix

| Provider | FunctionTools | SkillToolset |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub Models | ✅ | ✅ |
| Gemini | ✅ | ✅ |
| OpenRouter | ✅ | ✅ |
| HuggingFace | ✅ (model-dependent) | ✅ |
| OpenCode | ✅ (model-dependent) | ✅ |
| **Groq** | ❌ multi-tool fails | ❌ |
| **NVIDIA NIM** | ❌ multi-tool fails | ❌ |

# Agent Patterns Reference

## LlmAgent — conversational agent
- Primary pattern: wraps a model with a system instruction
- Can have Tools, Toolsets, OutputKey
- When OutputKey is set, final text response is stored to session state

## SequentialAgent — pipeline
- Runs SubAgents in order, one at a time
- State flows: `stage N sets OutputKey` → `stage N+1 reads {key}`
- Use for: code write → review, draft → edit → finalise

## LoopAgent — iterative refinement
- Runs SubAgents repeatedly until ExitLoopTool is called or MaxIterations hit
- MaxIterations is a safety cap, not the target
- Use for: draft → quality-check loops, consensus-building

## ParallelAgent — concurrent execution
- Runs all SubAgents concurrently in independent goroutines
- Each SubAgent gets its own state scope; results merged after all complete
- Use for: multi-perspective analysis, parallel fact-gathering

## Custom Run agent — arbitrary logic
- Implement `agent.Agent` interface with a custom `Run` method
- Can read/write session state directly, call sub-agents conditionally
- Use for: routing agents, state machines, non-LLM processing steps
- See `agents/llmauditor.go` for a reference implementation

## agenttool — agent-to-agent delegation
- Wraps an agent as a Tool so another agent can invoke it on demand
- See `agents/collaboration/` for multi-agent delegation patterns

---

# Session State Patterns

```go
// Read state inside a custom Run agent or tool
state := ctx.Session().State()
value, err := state.Get("my_key")
if err == nil {
    if s, ok := value.(string); ok {
        // use s
    }
}

// Count all state entries (for debugging)
count := 0
for range state.All() { count++ }

// Write state (prefer OutputKey; direct Set for non-LLM agents)
state.Set("my_key", "my_value")
```

---

# Skill System Reference

## SKILL.md format
```markdown
---
name: skill-name
description: One sentence — shown in list_skills output for LLM routing.
license: MIT
compatibility: google.golang.org/adk v1+
---

# Skill Title

Full instructions the LLM follows when this skill is loaded via load_skill.
Can include examples, constraints, output format requirements.
```

## Skill categories (current)
- `skills/agents/` — Agent roles: analyzer, comparator, grader
- `skills/collaboration/` — Multi-agent workflows: code-review, requesting/receiving review
- `skills/design/` — Design: consultation, review-feedback, plan-design-review
- `skills/documentation/` — Doc workflows: drafting, review, iteration, consensus, finalization
- `skills/engineering/` — Engineering: architecture, code-review, debug, go-expert, health,
  exitlooptool, refactor, test-driven, testing-strategy, system-design, tech-debt,
  terminal-assistant, incident-response, qa, standup

## SkillToolset tools
- `list_skills` — returns XML list of all available skills with name + description
- `load_skill {"name": "go-expert"}` — returns full SKILL.md instructions for a skill

## Schema patch requirement
The upstream `google.golang.org/adk/tool/skilltoolset` emits `{"type":"object"}` with no
`"properties"` key for `list_skills` args. OpenAI-compatible APIs (Groq, NVIDIA, etc.)
reject this with a 400 error. The local `tool/skilltoolset` wrapper fixes both
`list_skills` (empty properties) and `load_skill` (explicit name schema).

Always use `localskilltoolset.New(...)` — never the upstream directly.

---

# Pitfalls

## P1 — Missing jsonschema tag → silent tool failure

**Symptom**: Tool is registered but LLM never calls it, or calls it with
empty/wrong arguments.
**Root cause**: `jsonschema:""` tag is missing from args struct fields. The JSON
Schema sent to the LLM has no parameter descriptions, making parameters opaque.
**Fix**: Add `jsonschema:"Description text."` to every field in every args struct.
**Prevention**: Run a tool schema linter or always copy the canonical skeleton.

## P2 — OpenAI-compat schema rejection (empty properties)

**Symptom**: `list_skills` call returns HTTP 400 from Groq/NVIDIA/OpenRouter.
**Root cause**: `{"type":"object"}` schema with no `"properties"` key is invalid
per strict OpenAI schema validation.
**Fix**: Use `tool/skilltoolset` (local wrapper) — it injects `"properties": {}`.
**Prevention**: Never use the upstream `google.golang.org/adk/tool/skilltoolset`
directly — always go through the local wrapper.

## P3 — Groq multi-tool: tool_use_failed

**Symptom**: Groq agent returns `tool_use_failed` or garbled function-call JSON.
**Root cause**: Groq's LLaMA models mishandle prompts with multiple tool
declarations in the same request.
**Fix**: Remove all `Tools` and `Toolsets` from Groq/NVIDIA agent configs.
**Prevention**: Rule R4 — provider-specific agents get no tools.

## P4 — LoopAgent runs MaxIterations unconditionally

**Symptom**: Refinement loop always runs exactly MaxIterations even when the
LLM outputs "APPROVED" or equivalent.
**Root cause**: `exitlooptool.New()` is not in the reviewer agent's `Tools` list.
The LLM has no mechanism to signal loop termination.
**Fix**: Add `exitlooptool.New()` to the reviewer/checker agent inside the loop.
**Prevention**: Rule R5 — checklist item when creating any LoopAgent.

## P5 — Genkit import outside oaibridge

**Symptom**: Compile error "duplicate registration" or unexpected telemetry
behaviour; `init()` functions running twice.
**Root cause**: `firebase/genkit` registers global state in `init()`. Importing
it from multiple packages causes double registration.
**Fix**: Remove genkit import from the offending package; call `oaibridge.NewModel`
instead.
**Prevention**: Rule R6 — enforced by import boundary in ADR-0002.

## P6 — Duplicate OutputKey in SequentialAgent

**Symptom**: Stage N+1 output overwrites stage N output; earlier stage results
disappear from session state.
**Root cause**: Two agents in the same Sequential pipeline share the same `OutputKey`.
**Fix**: Rename keys to be unique and descriptive (e.g. `stage1_draft`, `stage2_review`).
**Prevention**: Rule R8 — prefix keys with stage name.

## P7 — Failover first-token latency

**Symptom**: Response takes significantly longer than expected when primary
provider is healthy.
**Root cause**: `failover.Model` always buffers the full response before forwarding
(ADR-0003). First-token latency = full round-trip time, not streaming latency.
**Fix**: This is by design. For latency-sensitive cases, use a single provider
directly (accepting reduced reliability).
**Prevention**: Document this trade-off clearly in product requirements.

## P8 — Echo model in production

**Symptom**: All agent responses are "I am the echo model and I received: ..."
**Root cause**: `ECHO_FALLBACK_ENABLED=1` was deployed in a non-dev environment.
**Fix**: Remove the env var from the deployment config.
**Prevention**: Rule R7 — add `ECHO_FALLBACK_ENABLED` to the forbidden env var list
in CI/CD production configs.

## P9 — nil failover chain (all providers unconfigured)

**Symptom**: First agent call panics or returns "no providers configured" error.
**Root cause**: All provider API keys are unset → all provider models are nil →
`failover.New` has an empty chain.
**Fix**: Set at least one API key. `make env` shows which are configured.
**Prevention**: Add a startup check that validates the chain has ≥1 provider.

## P10 — skills/ directory not found at runtime

**Symptom**: `list_skills` returns an empty list; skills are not available.
**Root cause**: The binary is run from a directory other than the repo root, so
`./skills` is not found by `os.Stat("./skills")`.
**Fix**: Always run from the repo root, or set a `SKILLS_DIR` env var pointing
to the absolute path of the `skills/` directory.
**Prevention**: Use `make run` which sets the working directory correctly.

---

# ADR Summaries

## ADR-0001: Use ADK as the agent layer
- **Decision**: `google.golang.org/adk` v1.2.0 as sole agent orchestration layer.
- **Why not Genkit flows**: Genkit's flow model is imperative and code-first; ADK provides declarative agent composition with built-in session, state, artifact management.
- **Why not custom**: ADK provides runner, session, event streaming, telemetry, launcher modes out of the box.

## ADR-0002: Genkit only for oaibridge
- **Decision**: Genkit v1.7.0 used only as an OpenAI-compatible HTTP client via `compat_oai`.
- **Boundary**: `model/oaibridge` is the only file that may import `firebase/genkit`.
- **Why**: Genkit's `compat_oai` is mature and handles auth, retry, and wire protocol. Avoids writing raw HTTP for 6+ providers.

## ADR-0003: Buffered failover
- **Decision**: `failover.Model.GenerateContent` always buffers the full response before forwarding.
- **Why**: Partial streaming responses cannot be retried transparently. Buffering allows clean provider switching on any error.
- **Trade-off**: Higher first-token latency in exchange for reliability.

## ADR-0004: Remove lipgloss JoinVertical
- **Decision**: Replaced `lipgloss.JoinVertical` with manual string joining in TUI rendering.
- **Why**: JoinVertical introduced subtle height calculation bugs with Glamour-rendered content.

## ADR-0005: Provider Config struct pattern
- **Decision**: Each provider package exposes `Config` struct + `ConfigFromEnv()` + `NewModel()`.
- **Why**: Consistent interface for all providers; easy to test; avoids global state; supports programmatic configuration.

## ADR-0006: SKILL.md + SkillToolset
- **Decision**: Skills are plain Markdown files discovered at runtime by SkillToolset.
- **Why**: Zero-code skill authoring; skills can be added/edited without recompiling; file-system-based discovery is transparent and debuggable.

## ADR-0007: SkillToolset schema patch
- **Decision**: Wrap upstream SkillToolset with schema-patched `list_skills` and `load_skill` tools.
- **Why**: OpenAI-compatible APIs reject `{"type":"object"}` with no `"properties"` key. The upstream ADK SkillToolset emits this for no-arg tools. The patch adds `"properties": {}` to satisfy strict validation.

---

# Run Modes

```sh
# Interactive terminal UI (Bubbletea)
make run            # go run ./cmd/tui chat
go run ./cmd/tui chat

# One-shot query (no TUI)
go run ./cmd/tui run "What is the weather in Bangkok?"

# ADK built-in text console
make console        # go run . console

# Browser dev-UI + REST API (http://localhost:8080)
make web            # go run . web webui api

# REST API only
make api            # go run . web api

# Genkit developer UI (requires Node.js)
make genkit-start

# Tests
make test           # go test ./...
make test-failover-echo   # failover test without real API keys
make test-failover-live   # failover test with real providers

# Build
make build          # go build ./...
make build-linux-amd64    # cross-compile CGO=0 linux/amd64
```

---

# Repository File Map

```
go-adk-q/
├── AGENTS.md                      # AI coding instructions (canonical)
├── llms.txt                       # Machine-readable project index
├── llms-full.txt                  # This file — full RAG context
├── main.go                        # ALL agent definitions + ADK launcher
├── Makefile                       # All targets; see §Run Modes
├── go.mod                         # module go-adk-q; go 1.24+
├── go.sum
│
├── cmd/tui/
│   ├── main.go                    # TUI binary, Cobra CLI, provider init
│   ├── chat.go                    # Bubbletea model, fillLines, paintLines
│   ├── markdown.go                # Glamour style per theme
│   ├── slash.go                   # Slash command autocomplete
│   ├── model_picker.go            # /model overlay
│   ├── settings.go                # /settings overlay
│   └── session.go                 # Session persistence
│
├── model/
│   ├── catalog/catalog.go         # ModelEntry, ProviderCatalog, Register()
│   ├── echo/echo.go               # Static-response stub (dev/CI only)
│   ├── failover/
│   │   ├── failover.go            # Buffered multi-provider failover
│   │   └── failover_test.go       # Mock-based unit tests
│   ├── oaibridge/bridge.go        # Genkit ↔ ADK type bridge
│   ├── githubmodels/              # GitHub Models (GPT-4o, LLaMA 4, etc.)
│   ├── groq/                      # Groq LPU inference (LLaMA 3.3)
│   ├── nvidia/                    # NVIDIA NIM (MiniMax M1)
│   ├── openrouter/                # OpenRouter (multi-provider routing)
│   ├── huggingface/               # HuggingFace Inference API
│   └── opencode/                  # OpenCode AI gateway (free tier)
│
├── tools/tools.go                 # get_weather, get_current_time FunctionTools
│
├── tool/skilltoolset/
│   └── skilltoolset.go            # Schema-patched list_skills + load_skill
│
├── skills/                        # SKILL.md files (auto-discovered)
│   ├── agents/                    # analyzer, comparator, grader
│   ├── collaboration/             # code-review, requesting/receiving review
│   ├── design/                    # design-consultation, design-review-feedback
│   ├── documentation/             # doc-drafting, doc-review, doc-iteration
│   └── engineering/               # go-expert, architecture, debug, code-review, etc.
│
├── agents/
│   ├── llmauditor.go              # Custom Run agent (quality auditor)
│   └── collaboration/             # agenttool delegation patterns
│
├── sample/                        # Standalone runnable examples
│   ├── groq/                      # Groq provider demo
│   ├── openrouter/                # OpenRouter model selection demo
│   └── opencodezen/               # Multi-agent collaboration demo
│
└── docs/                          # Diátaxis documentation
    ├── README.md                  # Navigation index
    ├── ai-memory/                 # AI context files (QUICK_CONTEXT, SYSTEM_PROMPT)
    ├── tutorials/                 # get-started, first-agent, add-provider
    ├── how-to/                    # add-agent, add-skill, add-theme, add-provider, debug-tui
    ├── reference/                 # config, cli, api, providers, themes
    ├── explanation/               # architecture, failover, tui-rendering, pitfalls
    └── adr/                       # ADR-0001 through ADR-0007
```
